relations.subject: server:node-removal
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate; independent corroboration, on its own dedicated page, of the same distinction first stated on fail-nodes-over.md
relations.evidence: When a node is flagged for _removal_ (as opposed to _failover_), new replica vBuckets will be created on the remaining nodes, as node-removal occurs. This has the effect of reducing available memory for the specified number of replicas.

relations.subject: server:node-removal
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate; a judgment call capturing that removal has no failover precondition at all, unlike recovery
relations.evidence: A node can be removed from the cluster by means of the CLI. Note that the node does not have to be _failed over_ prior to removal.

relations.evidence: Nodes can be _failed over_, so that an unhealthy or unresponsive node can be removed from the cluster without application-access being affected. See [Fail Nodes Over](fail-nodes-over.md).

notable_absence.finding: No role requirement is stated for node removal, consistent with every other operation in this batch except node-addition and node-join (which name Full/Cluster Admin) and modify-services (which names Full Administrator explicitly in its Prerequisites). Removal, arguably as consequential as addition, is left unstated.

cross_component_finding: This page's own framing sentence is the single cleanest statement in the whole batch of the 'one rebalance, many triggers' finding: 'The _rebalance_ operation distributes active and replica vBuckets across available cluster nodes in optimal fashion... Examples of using rebalance after node-addition have already been provided... Nodes can also be rebalanced following removal.' The mechanism is stated once, generically, and then simply invoked again for a different trigger - textual evidence that the docs themselves model rebalance as one operation, not a family.
